sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: An understory palm of wet forests in Colombia and northern Ecuador, with short subterranean or creeping stems. Its pinnate leaves may reach about 7 m. Inflorescences arise among the leaves and fruits form clusters. The leaf fibres are used for basketry and hat-making.

sections.title: Uses and safety
sections.text: Kew records food use but does not identify the plant part, so no specific edible part is stated here. This species is distinct from Phytelephas, the principal source of vegetable ivory in the documented trade.
